finder.title: Which test do I need?
finder.intro: Answer four questions to see the test that usually applies. Always confirm in the call for applications (bando) of your program.
finder.result.imat.text: The national test for medicine in English at public universities, at the end of September. You register on Universitaly.
finder.result.filter.text: No entrance test: you enrol in an open first semester and take three national exams. Registration usually opens in July on Universitaly.
finder.result.privmed.text: Each private university has its own test and ranking, usually between February and April. You can apply to several.
finder.result.tolc.text: Most public universities use a TOLC. The university decides which type (for example TOLC-I for engineering or TOLC-E for economics). Some programs have no test at all.
finder.result.cents: CEnT-S, or the university's own test
finder.result.cents.text: Many English-taught programs use CISIA's CEnT-S, which replaced the English TOLCs. Others assess your file or use their own test.
finder.result.private.text: Private universities set their own tests and dates. For example, Bocconi accepts its online test, the SAT or the ACT.
finder.result.masters: Usually no test: a file assessment
finder.result.masters.text: The university checks your degree, transcript, CV and language certificate. Some economics and management programs also ask for the GMAT or GRE.
timeline.title: Your year at a glance
timeline.intro: When each stage usually happens if you want to start in September or October. The stages overlap, so start early.
timeline.p1.text: Choose universities and cities, check the language requirements and start preparing for tests.
timeline.p2.text: Many universities open applications and pre-assessment, and most admission tests take place.
timeline.p3.text: Universities send their answers. Prepare your documents and pre-enrol on Universitaly.
timeline.p4.text: Book your consulate appointment early. Some tests, such as IMAT, are still in September.
timeline.p5.text: Enrol at the university and request your residence permit within 8 working days of arriving.
timeline.note: These are usual periods, not deadlines. Each university sets its own dates:
fees.title: Tuition fees by university
fees.intro: How much international students with family income abroad pay each year, at the universities we have checked. Universities with lower fees first, then those with higher fees.
fees.noFree.title: No university in Italy is completely free.
fees.noFree.text: Even where the university fee is low or zero, you usually pay a regional tax for the right to study (about €140 to €192) and a €16 stamp duty each year. A regional DSU scholarship can cover your fees, and students from particularly poor countries often pay less. The amounts below are for students with family income abroad; conditions apply, so always check the official page.
fees.lower.intro: Up to €5,000 a year at most. Mostly public universities, where the fee depends on your country or your family's income.
fees.higher.intro: More than €5,000 a year for at least some programmes. Mostly non-state universities, many of which offer scholarships and fee reductions.
fees.taxExtra: plus regional tax and stamp duty
fees.missing: We list only universities whose fees we could check on an official page. If your university is not here, look for its "tasse e contributi" page.

schol.card.palestinian.text: Italian university scholarships for students living in the Palestinian territories, and the situation of students from Gaza.
schol.card.refugee-italy.text: For people with international or temporary protection: MUR-CRUI, art and music schools (AFAM), Brescia, Turin, and the EQPR if you lost your documents.
schol.card.unicore.text: A master's degree in Italy for refugees living in some countries of Africa and South Asia, with UNHCR. The last call ran from 2 March to 17 April 2026.
schol.card.conflict: Scholarships for students from countries in conflict
schol.card.conflict.text: You do not always need refugee status: Politecnico di Torino, Turin, Florence, Palermo and Siena have offered scholarships.
schol.card.phd.text: Most PhD places come with a scholarship of at least €16,243 gross a year. See when each university's call closes.
schol.card.phd-risk: PhD places for candidates at risk
schol.card.phd-risk.text: Padova's PhD at Risk scholarships, and research fellowships from the Scholars at Risk network.
schol.card.dsu.text: Money, a place in a residence and meals, based on your family's income. International students can apply.
schol.card.maeci.text: For master's, PhD and research. The 2026/27 call closed on 26 March 2026.
schol.card.university.text: Many universities offer their own scholarships. See the scholarships directory.
